title: Refund Path and Clawback Terms by Gift Cards & Store Credit Type
content:
For every Gift Cards & Store Credit type, a refund of value spent from an instrument returns to that same instrument. The types differ in what becomes of a refund owed to an instrument that has already expired, and in whether value can be taken back after issue and up to what ceiling.

## Refund path

| Instrument type | Refund of value spent returns to the same instrument | Refund owed after the instrument has expired |
|---|---|---|
| Marlowe Rewards Note | Yes | A new Marlowe Rewards Note is issued for it |
| Bonus Gift Card | Yes | Forfeited |
| Goodwill Credit | Yes | Forfeited |
| Return Store Credit | Yes | Not applicable (the type never expires) |
| Marlowe & Finch Gift Card | Yes | Not applicable (the type never expires) |
| Marlowe & Finch e-Gift Card | Yes | Not applicable (the type never expires) |

## Clawback terms

| Instrument type | Value can be taken back after issue | Ceiling of a clawback |
|---|---|---|
| Marlowe Rewards Note | No | Not applicable |
| Bonus Gift Card | Yes | The current balance |
| Goodwill Credit | No | Not applicable |
| Return Store Credit | Yes | The current balance |
| Marlowe & Finch Gift Card | No | Not applicable |
| Marlowe & Finch e-Gift Card | No | Not applicable |

## Illustrations (hypothetical balances)

- A clawback of 30.00 is owed on a Return Store Credit whose current balance is 18.00: the ceiling is the current balance, so 18.00 is taken back.
- The same clawback owed on a Return Store Credit holding 45.00 is taken back in full, 30.00, since it does not exceed the current balance.
- No value is ever taken back from a Goodwill Credit, a Marlowe Rewards Note or a purchased gift card, because those types do not allow clawback.
